Intro.title: Spaces shaped by what they are made of, and by how they are lived in.
Intro.body1: etarq studio is an architecture and design practice based in Mexico City. Its projects range from retail interiors to coffee bars, stairs and planted passages, always built from honest, tactile materials: timber, stone, plaster, ceramic and living plants.
Intro.body2: Light, shade and vegetation are treated as part of the construction, not as decoration.

buna.title: Buna
buna.summary: A glazed-tile bar under a light steel canopy.
buna.description: A coffee counter clad in bronze-toned glazed tile sits beneath a red steel frame and a translucent canopy that filters daylight. A raw stone basin with a matte black tap anchors the counter, while planting surrounds the whole composition.

yale.title: Yale
yale.summary: Timber shelving and a stone-topped counter against a dark wall.
yale.description: A clothing store organised around a continuous timber display wall. Lit panels frame the brand mark, a stone-topped counter greets the visitor, and a charcoal wall carries a slogan in large lettering.

escalera.title: Stair & Garden
escalera.summary: A cantilevered concrete stair rising from an indoor garden.
escalera.description: Concrete treads fold in a zig-zag from the wall, finished with a timber handrail and slender steel balusters. At the foot, a bed of large-leaf plants brings green into a calm white hall with a pale stone floor and a strip of skylight above.

pergola.title: Pergola
pergola.summary: A timber-and-steel pergola threading through planters.
pergola.description: Black steel posts carry a grid of timber beams and translucent panels, filtering daylight onto a warm timber floor. Planters on both sides turn the passage into a garden corridor, open toward the trees beyond.

rojo.title: Red Interior
rojo.summary: A saturated red envelope around pale timber furniture.
rojo.description: Walls and ceiling painted in saturated red and pink frame a red-framed window to the street. Pale timber benches and low tables, beside a wall of framed pictures, keep the scale warm and human, lit by a neon sign and small lamps.

cactus.title: Cactus Corner
cactus.summary: A timber bench carrying a low desert garden, washed in amber light.
cactus.description: A built-in timber bench wraps the corner and doubles as a planter for cacti and succulents, lit from below by a thin LED line. The rough plaster walls glow a greenish gold, with a single spotlight and exposed joists overhead.

cocina.title: Green Skylight Kitchen
cocina.summary: A render of a kitchen under a planted timber lattice.
cocina.description: A rendered study of a kitchen where a planted timber lattice opens the ceiling to the sky, scattering dappled light across a terrazzo floor. Warm wood cabinetry, a stone island and lit niches complete a calm palette.

Maquette.title: Volumes in suspension
Maquette.body: An abstract study of volumes: spiralling stone steps, a timber-and-steel pergola, and planters. Turn the piece to see it from other angles.
Maquette.caption: Abstract study inspired by the stepped stone, the timber pergola and the green stair in the studio's work. It does not represent a built building.
Maquette.fallbackNote: The 3D view is not available on this device. Here is a photograph of the detail that inspires it.

Approach.title: Four ideas that run through the studio's work.
Approach.lead: A way of designing that starts from what is touched, seen and used every day.
Approach.draftNote: Draft wording based on the photographed projects; to be refined with the studio.

matter.title: Matter
matter.body: Timber, stone, plaster and ceramic are kept close to their natural state. Texture, grain and weight do the work that ornament usually does.

light.title: Light
light.body: Daylight is filtered, reflected and softened by pergolas, canopies and skylights; at night, warm low-level light draws the edges of each space.

green.title: Living green
green.body: Plants are planned from the first sketch: in planters, under stairs, along benches, through the ceiling. They are part of how a space is experienced, not an afterthought.

everyday.title: Everyday life
everyday.body: A coffee counter, a shop wall, a hallway stair: the studio designs the places where ordinary routines happen, at the scale of the hand and the step.
